note: Wellfleet Communications (Bedford, later Billerica MA), routers; merged with SynOptics in October 1994 to form Bay Networks (Santa Clara), which Nortel bought in June 1998 for $9.1B (Wikipedia). City is Bay Networks' last headquarters. NEA's first investment is 1990 (the firm's own year); no source read names the round.

Berkeley Networks, enterprise IP switches, headquartered in Milpitas CA (Wikipedia infobox); FORE Systems bought it in 1998 for about $250M. NEA's first investment is 1996 (the firm's own year); no source read names the round.

Bethesda Research Laboratories (Gaithersburg MD), molecular biology enzymes; merged with GIBCO in 1983 to form Life Technologies (Wikipedia, Life Technologies), the firm's exit line. NEA's first investment is 1980 (the firm's own year); no source read names the round.

BCD Semiconductor Manufacturing, analog and power ICs; principal executive offices in Minhang District, Shanghai (its 2008 F-1). The F-1's investors' rights agreement lists New Enterprise Associates 11 and NEA Ventures 2004 among the Series C Holders under the Series C Preference Shares Purchase Agreement of 2004-04-27, the firm's first-investment year; Series A and B preceded it, so the entry is Growth, as in the Redpoint row. Listed on Nasdaq (BCDS) in 2011, acquired by Diodes in 2013.

Bloom Energy (founded 2001 as Ion America), solid oxide fuel cells, headquartered in San Jose (Wikipedia). Market cap $82.48B as of 2026-09-30 (stockanalysis.com), which replaces the 2025-06-30 public float of $3.9B on file (the stock rose about 379% in a year): band 10b_plus. NEA 10 and NEA Ventures 2003 sign its registration rights agreement and the firm's first-investment year is 2003; no source read names the round NEA entered.
Black Diamond Therapeutics, precision oncology, headquartered in Cambridge MA (Nasdaq: BDTX); the Form D address in Stony Brook NY is its founding lab's.

Box, cloud content management, headquartered in Redwood City. The firm's first-investment year is 2008; its S-1 names New Enterprise Associates only among the holders its credit agreement permits, and no source read names the round NEA entered.
Bitglass, cloud access security broker (Campbell CA); acquired by Forcepoint in 2021, the firm's exit line. The Form D address is an earlier Palo Alto office.
Blue Cheetah Analog Design, die-to-die chiplet interconnect IP (Sunnyvale, the Form D address); acquired by Tenstorrent in 2025, the firm's exit line.

Brandless, direct-to-consumer essentials (San Francisco). It closed in February 2020 and its brand was bought and relaunched by new owners, read acquired under the asset-sale rule, aligned with the GV and Redpoint rows. The Form D band's Growth entry agrees with TechCrunch (2017-07-11, cited in the GV row): NEA and GV closed the $35M Series B.

Belly, merchant loyalty platform (Chicago). Wikipedia: in August 2013 Belly received a $12.1M Series B-1 round led by New Enterprise Associates, the firm's first-investment year; Lightbank's ~$3M seed and a16z's 2012 Series B came first, so the entry is Growth. In November 2018 the Belly product line assets were acquired from Hatch Loyalty by Mobivity Holdings (Wikipedia; the firm's exit line), so the row reads acquired under the asset-sale rule; the a16z row reads defunct and should align.

Boingo Wireless, Wi-Fi and DAS networks, founded in 2001 by Sky Dayton; taken private by Digital Colony (DigitalBridge) in 2021 for about $854M, and it moved its headquarters from Los Angeles to Frisco TX in December 2022 (Wikipedia). NEA 10 and NEA Ventures 2001 held 22.5% at the 2011 IPO (S-1); the S-1 shows Series A, A-2 and B preferred but does not tie NEA to a series, so the round is not on record.

Blue Ocean Smart System, chiplet-based AI chips for cloud and edge (the firm's description), founded 2019 and headquartered in Hsinchu, Taiwan, with R&D in Nanjing and Shanghai (its own release, 2021-07-12). The release says the A round was led by IDG Capital and ARM China and the A+ round by 'NEA Capital' and Henderson Capital in early 2021; NEA lists it with Carmen Chang on the board and a 2020 first investment, so the entry is the A+ extension, Series A. The General Catalyst and Insight rows named Blue Ocean are a different company (a San Francisco SaaS).

Basalt Health (basalt.health), EMR-integrated admissions software for post-acute care. The firm's own listing labels NEA's 2025 first investment Seed; the company then raised a $20M Series A led by NEA (Business Wire headline, 2026-09-24), a later round named Series A, so the row graduated. No valuation disclosed. The company's site and the headline give no city. The Y Combinator and General Catalyst rows named Basalt are a different company (satellite constellation software).

Backflip AI, generative AI for 3D design and CAD, founded December 2022 by Markforged's founders. TechCrunch (2024-12-19): a16z and NEA co-led the $30M Series A; an earlier seed is undisclosed and not tied to NEA, and the firm's first-investment year is 2024, so the entry is the Series A (the a16z row agrees). No valuation disclosed. Momentum slice checked 2026-09-30 (Google News, 'Backflip AI'): no later priced round, below $1B. City: neither the article nor the site states a headquarters (the careers page lists one San Francisco role).

Belong Health, Medicare Advantage and special-needs plans built with regional health plans, headquartered in Philadelphia (its release; the Form D address is Radnor PA). NEA led the $40M Series A (PR Newswire, 2021-12-15) with seed investor Maverick Ventures, the firm's first-investment year; Mohamad Makhzoumi joined the board. The entry date on file (2025-11-13) was read off a later Form D and is replaced by the Series A's. A 2025 Form D reports a further $58.3M offering; no valuation disclosed.

AviadoBio, gene therapies for frontotemporal dementia and ALS, spun out of the UK DRI at King's College London. At launch (UK DRI, 2021-12-01) it announced an $80M (GBP 58.6M) Series A led by NEA and co-led by Monograph Capital, after a $16.5M seed from Advent, the Dementia Discovery Fund, F-Prime and others; NEA's first-investment year is 2021, so the entry is the Series A. Astellas paid $50M in 2024 for an option on its lead program (Fierce Biotech), a licensing deal, not a mark; below $1B.

Bestow, term life insurance technology (Dallas). The firm's own listing labels its 2018 entry Growth, but the company's release (PR Newswire, 2018-05-21) says Valar Ventures led the $15M Series A 'with participation from existing investors New Enterprise Associates (NEA)', bringing total financing to just over $18M: NEA held a position from the roughly $3M raised before the Series A, a seed-sized round no page names (stage uncited, low). The Series A is a later round named Series A, so the row graduated. Series C $70M (December 2020); Series D $120M co-led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives and Smith Point Capital (TechCrunch, 2025-05-13), valuation undisclosed ('approximately doubled' since the Series C), so no figure bands the row: below $1B.

funding_rounds.lead: Goldman Sachs Alternatives; Smith Point Capital

note: BetterDoctor, provider directory data (San Francisco, the Form D address). Quest Analytics acquired it for an undisclosed amount (Healthcare Dive, 2018-06-19). NEA's first investment is 2014, the year of the company's one Form D ($10.4M, Mohamad Makhzoumi a director); no source read names that round, and the Form D band declined it (company incorporated 2011).

This row is Blend Therapeutics (Watertown MA, the Form D address; drug conjugates), NEA's 2011 biotech with James Barrett and Sheel Tyle as directors, not Blend Labs: the public status and the $696.5M float on file came from a join to the mortgage-software company and are removed. Blend Therapeutics was rebooted as Tarveda Therapeutics in 2016 (Endpoints, 2017-02-02) and Tarveda was liquidated in April 2022 after raising nearly $130M (Global Venturing, 2024-07-03, https://globalventuring.com/corporate/investment/fraud-debt-andlicensing-healthcare-startup-insolvencies/): defunct. The base also carries four Form D filings of Blend Systems, Inc. (CIK 1560253, Los Altos), another company. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Bliq GmbH, Berlin (its imprint, Lohmuehlenstrasse 65), an app that aggregates ride and delivery jobs for gig drivers; bliq.app now redirects to bliq.ai, which offers a driverless car subscription. NEA led the $13.5M Series A (Tech Funding News, 2022-05-11) with Speedinvest and others, after a EUR 2M seed in late 2020 (EU-Startups); NEA's first-investment year is 2022, so the entry is the Series A. No valuation disclosed.

Block Renovation, kitchen and bath renovation platform (New York). The firm's own listing labels its 2018 first investment Seed (the company launched in December 2018, The Real Deal). AlleyWatch (2021-07-26): a $40M Series B from NEA, Giant Ventures, Lerer Hippeau, Morningside and Obvious, $54M raised in total; a later round named Series B, so the row graduated. No valuation disclosed; a new CEO was appointed in January 2025 (PR Newswire).

BenchPrep, online learning platform for credentialing bodies and publishers (Chicago), founded 2009 as Watermelon Express. Wikipedia: in July 2012 it announced a $6M round from New Enterprise Associates and Revolution, the firm's first-investment year; no source read names that round. Built In Chicago (2019-01-15): a $20M Series C led by Jump Capital and Owl Ventures, $28.2M raised in total. Still operating (CEO interview, December 2024).

BeachMint, celebrity-curated subscription e-commerce (JewelMint, StyleMint; Santa Monica, the Form D address). After its board ousted the founders and returned $20M to investors (Business of Fashion, 2013-07-03), BeachMint combined with Conde Nast's Lucky magazine in August 2014 (New York Times, 'Lucky Magazine Gets an E-Partner to Shop With'), the firm's exit line 'Acquired by Conde Nast': a merger into another company, acquired. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

beehiiv, newsletter platform (New York). NEA's entry is the $33M Series B of April 2024 (Business Wire headline), which agrees with the Form D band; no valuation disclosed (a GetLatka estimate of $225M stays out, Rule A), and Google News on 2026-09-30 shows no later priced round: below $1B, as in the Lightspeed row.

Big Data Federation, Inc., machine-learning predictions of financial and economic fundamentals, incorporated 2015 and headquartered in San Jose (theorg.com; directory pages give 1735 Technology Drive), with an office in Moldova. The firm's own listing labels its 2019 entry Growth; Google News carries no round of the company, and no valuation is on record: below $1B.

BlueJeans Network, cloud video conferencing, headquartered at Santana Row, San Jose (Wikipedia), as in the Accel row; acquired by Verizon in 2020, which shut the service in 2023-24. Wikipedia: it had $23.5M from Accel, NEA and Norwest before its June 2011 launch, and NEA's first-investment year is 2011; no source read ties NEA to a named round.

Bluefish, marketing platform that measures and shapes how brands appear in AI answer engines (New York, its release dateline). The firm's own post (2025-08-20) announces 'our Series A investment in Bluefish' ($20M, AdExchanger), the firm's first-investment year. Threshold Ventures and NEA co-led the $43M Series B (PR Newswire, 2026-04-14), $68M raised in total; no valuation disclosed. Momentum check 2026-09-30 (Google News, 'Bluefish AI raises'): no $1B+ round, below $1B.

Blueshift, AI-driven customer data and marketing automation platform (San Francisco). The firm's own listing labels its 2014 first investment Seed. VentureBeat (2021-02-24): a $30M Series C led by Fort Ross Ventures and Avatar Growth Capital, $65M raised in total; a later round named Series C, so the row graduated. A $40M debt facility from Runway Growth followed in January 2024 (TechCrunch); no valuation on record, below $1B.

funding_rounds.lead: Fort Ross Ventures; Avatar Growth Capital

note: Boku, carrier billing and mobile payment methods, listed on London's AIM (BOKU). Wikipedia: Boku is headquartered in London, and its releases now carry London datelines; the a16z, Benchmark and Khosla rows read San Francisco, US (its home before the listing), so they should align. Wikipedia: after a $13M Series A (Khosla, Index, Benchmark) and DAG's $25M round in 2010, Boku raised $35M 'led by NEA and existing venture capital investors' (reported for 2012); the firm's own listing labels its 2011 entry Growth, which agrees, and the firm's year stands as the entry year. AIM market cap in the GBP 450-700M range per the Benchmark row's check: below $1B.

Bonsai, a platform for building and training industrial AI models (Berkeley CA, Electronics Weekly). Microsoft, an investor, bought it in June 2018 (Business Insider headline). Electronics Weekly (2017-05): a $7.6M round with Microsoft Ventures, NEA, ABB, Samsung NEXT and Siemens, $13.6M raised in total; NEA's first-investment year is 2014 and no source read names the earlier $6M or ties NEA to it. The Y Combinator row named Bonsai is a different company (freelancer software).

Brale, regulated fiat-backed stablecoin issuance platform (Des Moines, as in the Lightspeed row). The firm's own listing labels its 2022 first investment Seed, with Scott Sandell on the board. Lightspeed's own company page records its entry in Brale's Series A in 2025, a later round named Series A, so the row graduated. No valuation on record; below $1B.

BNTO, AI-driven fashion subscription across rental, resale and new (bnto.com). The firm's own listing labels its 2021 first investment Seed (Carmen Chang). WWD headline (2025-10-13): 'BNTO Launches AI Styling Agent and Secures $15 Million in Series A Funding', a later round named Series A (body paywalled), so the row graduated. No valuation disclosed. Neither the site nor the visible coverage states a headquarters city.

BoxC, API-first cross-border e-commerce logistics platform (boxc.com, still live). The firm's own listing labels its 2014 first investment Seed. Google News carries no round of the company and its site states no headquarters city. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Bloomreach, commerce search and marketing platform (Mountain View). Mark: the $175M round led by Goldman Sachs Asset Management at a $2.2B valuation (its release, 2022-02-23), stale beyond 24 months; no newer priced round found, as in the Bain Capital Ventures and Lightspeed rows. Stage: Lightspeed's own page records its entry at the Series B in 2010, and NEA's first investment is 2012, so NEA came in at a later round, Growth; no source read names it (the firm's 2012 post on 'SaaS 3.0' features the company).

Branch Metrics, mobile deep linking and attribution (Mountain View per Wikipedia; its 2022 release and Form D give Palo Alto). NEA's Scott Sandell in the company's release (2022-02-10): 'Since the day I met Alex, Mike, Mada and Dmitri during the seed investment'; Wikipedia dates that round, a $3M round led by NEA, to September 2014, the firm's first-investment year. The Form D band's Series A entry (2015) read the next round, disputed. Wikipedia: a $15M Series A in February 2015 followed, so the row graduated. Mark: the $300M Series F led by NEA at a $4B valuation (2022-02-10), stale beyond 24 months. The 8VC and a16z rows named Branch are Branch International, a different company (emerging-market lending).

Baihe (baihe.com), Chinese online dating and matchmaking, Beijing; it absorbed Jiayuan in 2015 and traded on China's New Third Board. In May 2018 Fosun chairman Guo Guangchang agreed to take about 70% of it through Yuanhong Investment (Global Dating Insights, 2018-05-04), a change of control read with the firm's exit line ('Acquired by Shanghai Huanzhuo') as acquired. NEA's first investment is 2006; no source read names the round.

Barkly, endpoint protection (Boston, the Form D address). Alert Logic acquired it in 2019; barkly.com now redirects to LevelBlue's 'Alert Logic is now LevelBlue' page. The Form D band's Series A entry (2015, Harry Weller a director) stands.

BrainCells Inc., San Diego (Form D address), repositioning compounds for central nervous system diseases; the firm listed it only in its 2013 archive. Its last Form D is dated 2011-12-29 ($4.1M sold of $9M); Google News carries nothing on the company, so its fate is not established. The Pre-Seed entry on file rests on a $135K 2009 filing of a company that was already venture-backed; a later pass should check its round history.

Berkshire Grey, AI robotic fulfillment (Bedford MA, Boston Globe 2023-03-24). Listed through the RAAC SPAC in July 2021, then taken private by SoftBank, which completed the purchase of the shares it did not own in July 2023. NEA 15 and NEA Ventures 2016 held 17.2% at the merger (8-K, 2021-07-27) and the firm's first-investment year is 2016; no source read names the round NEA entered (Khosla seeded it in 2013).

Braintree, online and mobile payments (Chicago). The firm's own listing labels its 2012 entry Growth, which agrees with the record: Accel led the $34M first round in 2011 (the Accel row) and Braintree raised $35M in October 2012 (WSJ, 2012-10-17), NEA's round (Rick Yang). eBay's PayPal bought it for $800M in September 2013 (the firm's own post, 2013-09-26).

Boulder Wind Power, direct-drive wind turbine generators (Boulder, the Form D address); it wound down operations in October 2014 (Wind Power Monthly, 2014-10-30). The Form D band's Series A entry (2009, Harry Weller and Ravi Viswanathan directors) stands.

Beyond Identity, passwordless phishing-resistant authentication (New York, the Form D address). Mark: the $100M Series C led by Evolution Equity Partners at a $1.1B valuation (SecurityWeek, 2022-02-22), stale beyond 24 months; no later priced round found. The Form D band's Series A entry agrees with the firm's own post (2020-04-14): NEA led the Series A with co-lead KDT.

BlockCypher, blockchain web services and developer APIs (Redwood City). The firm's own listing labels its 2014 first investment Seed. Google News shows the company operating (2015, 2018) but no later round. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

BedRocket Media, later SportsRocket, digital sports video networks and an OTT platform (New York, the Form D address). Coverage runs to 2017 (Sportsrocket Turbine, Sports Video Group and Forbes) and its last Form D is from 2018; sportsrocket.com now serves an empty page and the firm lists the investment as Past, so its fate is not established. The Form D band's Series A entry (2012, Patrick Kerins a director) stands.
